slot.brief: A projectile explodes or a ball thrown from a tower with given conditions; use two equations to find time of flight and range, with an intermediate point asked.

stem: A ball is projected horizontally from a tower and lands $60$ m from its base after $3$ s. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, how far horizontally has it travelled when it is $20$ m below its launch level?

verdicts.working: Horizontal speed = 60/3 = 20 m/s. A 20 m drop takes t = √(2×20/10) = 2 s, so horizontal distance = 20×2 = 40 m.

working:
$v_x=\dfrac{60}{3}=20$ m s$^{-1}$\n$20=\dfrac{1}{2}(10)t^2\Rightarrow t=2$ s\n$x=v_xt=20(2)=40$ m

Independent check: Horizontal speed = 60/3 = 20 m/s. A 20 m drop takes t = √(2×20/10) = 2 s, so horizontal distance = 20×2 = 40 m.
solution: The horizontal speed is $v_x=\dfrac{60}{3}=20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. For a vertical drop of $20$ m, $$20=\frac12(10)t^2\Rightarrow t=2\,\text{s}.$$ Hence $x=v_xt=20(2)=40$ m.

draft.stem: A ball is projected horizontally from a tower and lands $60$ m from its base after $3$ s. Taking $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$, how far horizontally has it travelled when it is $20$ m below its launch level?
draft.distractor_notes: A: uses the vertical displacement as the horizontal distance. B: uses half the total flight time. D: gives the full range rather than the distance at the specified point.
